items.title: Announcing Rust 1.100.0
items.summary: release, rust
items.content:
The Rust team is happy to announce a new version of Rust, 1.100.0. Rust is a programming language empowering everyone to build reliable and efficient software.

If you have a previous version of Rust installed via rustup , you can get 1.100.0 with:

If you don't have it already, you can get rustup from the appropriate page on our website, and check out the detailed release notes for 1.100.0 .

If you'd like to help us out by testing future releases, you might consider updating locally to use the beta channel ( rustup default beta ) or the nightly channel ( rustup default nightly ). Please report any bugs you might come across!

After 10 years and 5 failed stabilization attempts, the never type is finally stable ! This also completes the project goal for this work.

The never type, spelled ! in code, is the canonical uninhabited type. It represents the type of diverging computations – computations which never resolve to any value – where any code that follows is unreachable. Expressions that terminate control flow, such as return , break , and std::process::exit , also have the type ! .

Since having a value of the never type is impossible, Rust permits a never-to-any coercion, allowing to turn ! into any other type (this is what distinguishes it from any other uninhabited types). This can be used, for example, to not return a value from one of the branches of a match or an if :

While the never type could already be used and observed this way, and even named in the return type of functions ( -> ! ), this release allows naming the never type anywhere:

Additionally this release changes Infallible to be an alias to the never type. That makes all old APIs that used Infallible be compatible with using ! . This was the plan ever since the introduction of Infallible and is one of the reasons why the never type stabilization was so hard (waffle gave a talk about some of the troubles of the stabilization).

Unfortunately, to allow changing Infallible , we had to introduce a breaking change. This release changes the "never type fallback" from () to ! in editions before 2024 (i.e. 2015, 2018, and 2021), similarly to what has already been done in edition 2024 . This should largely be unnoticeable, but can affect code in some rare cases (for example when ignoring a result of a function returning a generic parameter). Note that this change might also make the compiler detect more code as unreachable.

We tried to minimize the impact of this breaking change as much as possible, by providing future compatibility warnings far in advance and releasing fixes to public crates that have been broken by this. If a dependency is failing due to issues with the never type, consider updating it, as a fix might have already been released for it.

This release brings about the stabilization of the core parts of allocator_api , enabling library authors to define custom allocators that can be used together with certain standard library types - currently Vec and Box . These are enabled through the newly-stabilized Allocator trait.

This is the foundation of the Allocators 1.0 project goal . A lot remains to be done still, including expanding the API surface usable with custom allocators and stabilizing their use on more collections and pointer types; with the core trait and design out of the way though, expect to see more being stabilized soon!

The Drop trait in Rust makes it possible to run code when a variable goes out of scope, regardless of whether we return , ? , or panic. Drop being a part of types means that in Rust you never have to close a socket .

Implementing Drop can however feel a little inconvenient when all you want is to run some code unconditionally when a function exits. This is why we’re introducing core::mem::DropGuard : a new helper type that runs a closure when dropped.

items.title: New York City Council Approves Landmark Legislation Banning Surveillance Pricing
items.content:
New York City Council Approves Landmark Legislation Banning Surveillance Pricing

Speaker Julie Menin’s legislation will prevent companies from using personal data to offer different prices to different New Yorkers

Council also passes legislative package in honor of Veterans Day, including property tax exemption for seriously disabled veterans

NEW YORK – Today, the New York City Council approved major legislation that will ban surveillance pricing in the five boroughs. The bill, sponsored by Speaker Julie Menin, will prevent companies from using New Yorkers’ personal data and algorithms to sell goods and services at different prices to different consumers, and is among the strongest surveillance pricing bans in the country.

In honor of Veterans Day, the Council also approved a package of bills aimed at improving life for New York City veterans. The package includes two bills that will improve housing access and affordability for veterans: one granting a full property tax exemption for the primary residence of permanently and totally disabled veterans, and the other requiring the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) to conduct an annual report on veteran occupancy in city-run Mitchell-Lama housing. A third bill in the package would establish a permanent LGBTQ+ liaison within the Department of Veterans’ Services (DVS).

Watch Speaker Menin’s pre-Stated press conference here and the Council’s Stated Meeting here . Photos will be available here .

Banning Surveillance Pricing in New York City

Introduction 891-A, sponsored by Speaker Julie Menin, would prohibit any entity or service provider from engaging in surveillance pricing, defined as pricing set completely or in part by algorithm that uses personal data to offer different prices to different customers for the same goods or services.

“The City Council is putting consumers first by ending the deceptive and insidious practice of surveillance pricing,” said Speaker Julie Menin. “When corporations use algorithms and personal data to charge different people different prices for the same products, it’s unethical and worsens our affordability crisis. We take consumer protection extremely seriously, and we will continue fighting to lower prices and stop predatory corporate tactics.”

Surveillance pricing is invisible to consumers, making it difficult to identify, but reports suggest the practice is occurring in a variety of industries. One investigation found that a major grocery delivery platform was engaging in algorithmic pricing experiments that resulted in individualized price differences as high as 23 percent. Another investigation found that the price of a television at one retailer increased from $499.99 to $599.99 when the consumer pulled into the store’s parking lot. A behavioral economist who worked for a major ride-share company revealed that the application increases prices when a consumer’s phone battery is low because they might not otherwise be able to get home if they do not accept the high offer. The Council aims to end these predatory practices and protect New York consumers with this landmark ban.

Introduction 1051-A, sponsored by Council Member Frank Morano, would provide that the primary residence of any permanently and totally disabled veteran shall be fully exempt from taxation and special district charges, assessments and special ad valorem levies, provided that such veteran meets all other applicable requirements of section 458-a of the real property tax law.

“On Veterans Day, we thank the men and women who served our country,” said Council Member Frank Morano. “The very next day, we’re backing up those words with action. New York State has already given local governments the authority to eliminate property taxes for veterans who are 100 percent disabled as a result of their military service, and it’s about time New York City did its part. These men and women have sacrificed enough, and they shouldn’t have to worry about being…

items.title: Diesel 2.4.0
items.content:
Diesel 2.4.0 includes contributions from 76 people. Over a span of 14 months, more than 1337 commits were submitted.

This release introduces several large new features to Diesel and also expands the number of platforms on which you can run Diesel out of the box. Notable changes include:

Besides these headline features, a significant amount of work was done to improve the robustness of the existing code. As part of this effort, we started fuzzing parts of Diesel and added support to run several tests using Miri and various sanitizers. This work helped uncover and fix various soundness and correctness issues, as well as bugs that could lead to panics. Most of the relevant fixes have already been backported to the various Diesel 2.3.x releases over the last few months.

Check out the full change log for a complete list of changes.

This release would not have been possible without the support of our contributors and sponsors. We would like to especially call out Prototype Fund for funding the development of the newly added support for views. We would also like to call out the Rust Foundation for recently sponsoring maintenance work on Diesel.

Nevertheless, the Diesel project is always looking for support. You can help by:

Diesel 2.4 introduces support for database views. It was already possible to use database views in previous versions of Diesel by manually writing table! definitions for your views and carefully only using methods that work with a particular view. Diesel 2.4 now introduces a view! macro that can be used to declare the existence of a database view. The syntax and usage of this macro closely mirror the existing table! macro, but the generated code prevents usage in any query other than SELECT statements.

Additionally, diesel-cli has been extended to support generating these view! definitions when you regenerate your schema.rs file via diesel print-schema or by running a new migration. Support for generating view! macro definitions can be enabled for existing projects by setting print_schema.include_views = true in your diesel.toml file. For new projects, this will be the default.

Finally, there is a new unstable print_schema.experimental_infer_nullable_for_views boolean configuration that enables inferring whether a view column might contain NULL values or not in more cases. By default, this configuration is disabled, causing Diesel to assume that most columns might contain NULL values, as reported by the underlying database system. This configuration enables an additional inference step to parse and verify the structure of relevant views to more accurately report possible null values. See this blog post from last year for more details. The underlying functionality is also available via a new diesel_infer_query crate for third parties. Since we still consider the results of this inference to be non-100% satisfying, this configuration is marked as experimental, meaning results might change in future Diesel versions. If you encounter a case that doesn’t work correctly, please report it in our issue tracker.

We would like to thank Prototype Fund again for funding the development of this feature.

Adding better support for mapping Rust enums to SQL values has been a long-standing request for Diesel. While such a mapping was possible for a long time, it either required significant custom code or the usage of a third-party crate. With Diesel 2.4, we finally introduce a new #[derive(Enum)] proc-macro to simplify the mapping of field-less Rust enums to SQL values.

This macro enables mapping a Rust enum to SQL side enum types (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB), integer fields (all backends), or text fields (all backends), depending on your database backend.

You can also use #[diesel(sql_types)] multiple times on the same enum to support mapping to several different types.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임받을 이용자가 [매니저 위임 신청] 버튼으로 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 활동 중인 부매니저가 있으면 부매니저만, 부매니저가 없거나 모두 부재중이면 회원이 신청할 수 있습니다.

신청하면 갤러리 공지로 신청 글이 등록되고, 신청일로부터 7일간 찬성 댓글을 받은 뒤 운영자가 검토해 위임합니다. 첫 번째 위임 신청자가 신청한 날로부터 7일간 3명까지 동시 신청이 가능합니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 2개, 댓글 4개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 1일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.content_ko: Apache DataSketches C++의 범위 외 쓰기 취약점이다. 신뢰할 수 없는 출처에서 KLL 스케치를 역직렬화하는 애플리케이션은, 직렬화된 레벨 경계 값이 검증되지 않아 조작된 스케치에 의해 힙 메모리가 손상될 수 있다. 영향을 받는 버전은 2.0.0부터 5.3.0까지다. 이 문제는 5.3.1 버전에서 수정됐으며 업그레이드가 권장된다. 원문에 표시된 CVSS 점수는 0.0(NA)이고 원격 악용 가능 여부는 False다. 공개일은 2026-11-13이다.

items.title: How Not to Build a Music Player
items.summary: person, zig
items.content:
The Twelve-Day War made me realize online music players aren’t a viable option for those who live under an oppressive regime that disconnects the internet across the country as a way to silence public opinion.

So, as soon as the connection came back, I started archiving tracks and looking for offline alternatives and discovered Strawberry . It’s a feature-rich music player and kept me happy for quite a while, but I have this habit of looking at song lyrics and singing along! Strawberry fetches lyrics from the internet when it recognizes a song, but sometimes the lyrics weren’t line-synced and worse, it displayed the timestamps next to the lyrics which I found pretty annoying to look at. I wasn’t aware of other music players such as foobar2000 which my friend just pointed me to while writing this post.

I decided to write my own music player and call it AMP with a few goals in mind: minimal feature-set, no C++ dependencies, proper system integration to make it feel like a native app, and of course, write it in Zig (including the shaders!). I also wanted to roll my own UI because of the fun memories of working on V’s UI during my first days of being introduced into system programming. But before I could make any meaningful progress, a new wave of protests started. Following the tragedy of January 8 and 9 , another internet blackout began, lasting more than four months.

During the blackout, there were these anonymous people on Telegram selling internet access through personal White SIMs , whitelisted servers, Starlink dishes, etc. A black market had formed for the freaking internet! You’d get charged $5 or more for just 1GB of traffic. The prices dropped slightly after a while, but it was still hella expensive. The regime surely made a lot of money out of it. I ended up spending hundreds of dollars on these services and other methods just to stay in touch with my friends and keep my hobbies alive. Killing time was becoming a problem. Especially for someone like me who built their entire social life online.

I carefully used this slow connection to download repositories, documention, etc. to continue working on my music player. It really brought me immense joy during this hard time.

Once the connection was mostly restored to the pre-blackout days (UDP traffic is still blocked, though, which naturally also affects QUIC), my attention was shifted towards LLMs. It had become very hard for me to ignore the hype and progress around frontier LLMs. As I really never thought about using them seriously for coding. They are still everywhere in the news, and I was just reminded that I owned a Claude Max 20x subscription gift from my boss back in 2025. Eating dust and maybe soon expiring. So I decided to give it a try and experiment on my music player. It was a very addictive experience. I literally couldn’t hit the plan limits no matter how hard I tried, so after a few non-stop days of prompting, a good chunk of AMP was vibecoded..

At the time, I thought this was an okay approach for a hobby project and I could just un-slopify it later. Little did I know I’m mentally incapable of reviewing tens of thousands lines of code. Shortly after, Anthropic figured that I live in Iran and instantly banned my account. Then Codeberg announced its no-AI policy , which gave me two choices. Either get rid of all that slop or move the repository elsewhere. Going with the former option, I started reading every single line of code, rewriting them. I was surprised by my own ignorance and how much LLMs like to complicate stuff. (I wish I could show an example, but my memory is extremely fragile and I’ve got no pre-rewrite history of the repo to check).

Four months later, nearly half the codebase is gone, and somehow it’s more robust with the same set of features (and more). I regret relying on LLMs in the first place, but hey, lesson learned. That said I think it’s still possible to create a healthy relationship with LLMs as long as you look at them as a…

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. We cannot yet be certain when the agent understood it was taking real world action, or to what extent it believed it was in a fictional test scenario; our analysis so far presents a…

items.title: Class Action Lawsuit Claims Honda Keyless Entry Systems Leave Certain Cars ‘Especially Vulnerable’ to Theft
items.content:
Innarella v. American Honda Motor Co., Inc. et al.

Filed: October 29, 2026 ◆ § 2:26-cv-12679

A class action lawsuit claims that certain vehicles equipped with Honda’s passive keyless entry system are especially vulnerable to theft.

Defendant(s) American Honda Motor Company, Inc. Honda Motor Company Ltd.

Law(s) California Consumers Legal Remedies Act

Categories Automotive Defective Products False Advertising Fraud

New to ClassAction.org? Read our Newswire Disclaimer

A proposed class action lawsuit claims that certain vehicles equipped with Honda’s passive keyless entry (PKE) system are “especially vulnerable” to theft, posing serious security issues that the automaker has allegedly ignored for years and failed to disclose to the public.

Get class action lawsuit and class action settlement news sent to your inbox – sign up for ClassAction.org’s free weekly newsletter .

The 77-page lawsuit against American Honda Motor Co., Inc. and Honda Motor Co., Ltd. accuses the companies of failing to disclose material information about the PKE system vulnerabilities, which have reportedly made certain Honda and Acura vehicles among the top-20 most stolen cars for the 2022-2024 model years in the United States. Per the filing, Honda has known for at least the last 15 years that the PKE systems at issue can be easily exploited yet has not offered anti-theft products, such as stealth immobilizers, for aftermarket sale at authorized dealerships or informed drivers that such products are available.

The class action lawsuit was filed amid an apparent surge in the exploitation of PKE systems by thieves nationwide. According to the case, the response to the theft epidemic from automakers has been “so lethargic” that U.S. Senator Edward Markey issued letters to 17 manufacturers , including Honda, seeking information regarding their keyless entry systems and what efforts, if any, have been taken to address the problem.

The complaint also mentions that in April 2026, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia unsealed a 15-count indictment and brought charges against six people for their alleged role in an international auto theft ring involving at least 20 cars in the D.C. metro area and Pennsylvania. According to the suit, the vehicles involved in the theft ring were “primarily recently manufactured Honda Civics and CRVs and Acura TLXs and RDXs” with keyless entry systems, which were allegedly exploited via electronic devices that enabled the perpetrators to reprogram the cars to accept previously blank key fobs. From the complaint:

“As the U.S. Attorney stated at a press conference: ‘They don’t need keys and they don’t need hot wiring. No smashed windows. No Drama. Just a sleek electronic device called an Autel,’ and in ‘under a minute, the car’s brain is rewritten, and the car is gone in 60 seconds.’ Thieves disconnect the GPS and the Bluetooth on the car, load the vehicles on transport carriers, and ship them overseas.”

According to the suit, the methods used by thieves to exploit the Honda PKE systems include relay theft, electronic software entry theft, Rolling-PWN attacks and key cloning theft.

The filing says that relay theft occurs when an individual uses an antenna to amplify the encrypted signal transmitted from a nearby key fob, with the boosted signal tricking the car into believing the key fob is nearby and allowing entry. Upon gaining entry, a thief will plug a device into the vehicle’s unsecured on-board diagnostic (OBD) port to code a new key, the suit states.

Electronic software entry theft occurs when a thief, with the aid of a laptop and software freely available for purchase online, nears a Honda or Acura with a PKE system and then uses the software to send a signal to “awaken” the car’s security system and open its doors, the lawsuit continues. items.title: Where to follow more Linux news without the clickbait
items.content:
Where to follow more Linux news without the clickbait

12 Nov 2026 at 8:15 am UTC | Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 at 2:32 pm UTC

Want more Linux news in your life? There's plenty worth reading and watching without being told Windows is dead for the fifteenth time this week. Here are some good places to start.

Before we dive in, remember you can follow GamingOnLinux on Telegram , WhatsApp , Fluxer , Discord , Bluesky and Mastodon . Pick your favourite and come join us!

Remember - a lively headline is fine to pull you in, but it should still match the story. One person breaking their desktop doesn't mean yours is about to explode - there's a lot of ridiculous clickbait out there. We're a big believer in healthy community building so these picks are those who generally steer away from such silliness.

LWN.net gets into the details of Linux development, security and the free software community. It can get technical, but it’s great for understanding why something is changing and what developers are discussing. Some articles require a subscription for immediate access.

Phoronix is a useful stop for hardware support, graphics drivers, kernel changes and benchmarks. If you enjoy checking how the latest AMD or Intel hardware performs on Linux, there are plenty of graphs waiting for you. You may want to avoid the comment section though.

OMG! Ubuntu covers Ubuntu, desktop Linux, apps and GNOME extensions in an approachable way. You don’t need to run Ubuntu to find something useful here, especially if you enjoy discovering little improvements for your desktop.

Linuxiac covers distributions, desktop environments and open-source software releases. Handy for keeping track of what’s new without spending your afternoon digging through release announcements.

9to5Linux follows distribution releases, desktop environments, kernel updates and Linux apps. Its weekly roundup is particularly useful when you’ve been busy actually using your computer and want to catch up on what you missed.

Project updates are worth following too. KDE's announcements and This Week in GNOME give you news straight from the people building the software, including new features, fixes and things still taking shape.

This Week in Linux is Michael Tunnell's Linux and open-source news roundup. A handy way to catch up with a cuppa, with links available when a story sends you down a rabbit hole.

The Linux Experiment is Nick's channel covering Linux news, desktop software, privacy and opinion. There’s a good mix of updates and explanations, plus a longer podcast if you finish a video and still want more Linux chat.

Gardiner Bryant covers Linux, gaming and free software, making his channel worth a look if Steam Deck and Linux gaming are your thing. Expect news mixed with personal takes and enthusiasm for the subject.

Learn Linux TV is Jay LaCroix's home for practical tutorials, distribution reviews and hardware coverage. It leans more towards learning than news, so it’s a useful companion when you’ve read about something and now want to see how it works.

Veronica Explains is the "Linux Mom", a sysadmin and COBOL lady posting videos about cool things you can do with Linux and a whole lot of retro too.

Destination Linux brings a weekly show full of showing off their passion for Linux and open source with various guests. Covering a big mixture of news across Linux, open source, interviews and more.

If you have other good sources of non-clickbait Linux news, feel free to leave a comment with your picks. They may even get added to this guide. However, as with any guide there is an element of bias here on who I choose to highlight based on how they present their articles and videos.

items.title: The anti-marketing aspect of the Gemini network
items.summary: web
items.content:
The anti-marketing aspect of the Gemini network

I like Gemini. Not the Google Chatbot but the network that existed before Google named its product. If you are enough of a geek, you may want to give it a try.

Creating a Blog in Gemini:// (brennan.day)

Eoin is counting the number of "capsules" on the Gemini network. A capsule is the equivalent of a "website" on the Web or a "hole" on Gopher. It’s a personal space, a bunch of pages. Blogs become "gemlogs".

Eoin’s first observation is that the number of active capsules is slowly growing. The network is healthy.

But his second observation is really interesting: there’s absolutely no correlation between the number of new capsules in a given month and articles about the Gemini protocol being promoted on the first page of Hacker News.

This is a confirmation of what I’ve benn trying to explain for years: your metrics and web statistics are completely useless. The number of visitors, the number of clicks are worthless if you are not a marketer trying to extract money from a big brand. They don’t mean anything.

By the way: you should really avoid Hacker News these days. The front page is heavily manipulated to promote pro-AI stuff and bury everything that might question wether fascism-capitalism is good.

Why is Hacker News like that? (drewdevault.com)

A Mozilla employee is leaving after 15 years and comes to a similar conclusion. Mozilla is awesome because it has always been abnormal. It is mostly used by abnormal people. This means that hiring "normal managers" who try to make it "normal" and chase "normal" metrics is, of course, a recipe for failure.

jr conlin's ink stained banana (blog.unitedheroes.net)

I always failed to understand those marketing people who try to be "like others but a bit cheaper". While all the value is being different enough to nurture your own niche.

I completely removed statistics from my blog in 2013. At the time, I had a very strong realisation that the blog posts that mattered most, those I was proudest of, and those that prompted people to mail me even years later all had mediocre statistics.

How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Web (ploum.net)

On the contrary, most of my hit, my "buzz", were quickly forgotten. But, being addicted to statistics, I was unconsciously adapting my writing style to improve those numbers. I was scrolling through social media posts that were highly popular while trying to create some myself.

Closing my social media accounts and, instead, procrastinating on Gemini had the opposite effect: making me read other ideas without caring about reactions, about popularity. Jsreed5 made the same observation while he was trying the Nostr protocol. While Nostr’s technicalities may be interesting by themselves, the content on it is similar to the one found of mainstream social networks. And our smolnet Gemini-formatted brains cannot take it anymore!

A Geminaut's View of Nostr (jsreed5.org)

We really need a simple Gemini hosting provider that would also provide a Web version, to welcome less technical-minded people who still may want to access a quieter, non-commercial, out-of-time virtual space.

Lot of people are trying Gemini and find that there’s no content on it, that they can’t have their news and dopamine hit on it. Well, that’s exactly the point.

There Is No Content on Gemini (ploum.net)

The fact that only a niche minority want to use it is also part of the point. Gemini might no be for you. That’s fine. The modern Web and even the real world (where every device is actively working against me and every human interaction seems to be about AI) is increasingly not for me. So let me have my strange niche space.

items.title: The entirety of "Let Over Lambda" is now freely available online
items.summary: book, lisp
items.content:
Let Over Lambda (ISBN 978-1-4357-1275-1, 376+iv pp.) is one of the most hardcore computer programming books out there. Starting with the fundamentals, it describes the most advanced features of the most advanced language: C OMMON L ISP . The point of this book is to expose you to ideas that you might otherwise never be exposed to.

This book is about macros, that is programs that write programs. Macros are what make lisp the greatest programming language in the world. When used properly, macros enable amazing feats of abstraction, programmer productivity, and code efficiency and security that are unheard of elsewhere. Macros let you do things you simply cannot do in other languages.

If you are looking for a dry coding manual that re-hashes common-sense techniques in whatever langue du jour, this book is not for you. This book is about pushing the boundaries of what we know about programming. While this book teaches useful macro skills that can help solve your programming problems today and now, it has also been designed to be entertaining and inspiring. If you have ever wondered what lisp or even programming itself is really about, this is the book you have been looking for.

2026 update: Let Over Lambda was published in 2008, to align with the 50th anniversary of Lisp's invention in 1958. A lot has changed since then, in both Lisp and programming practice in general. Although my thinking and opinions have evolved since, I still believe the book holds up well as a tutorial and explanation of why Lisp so special. Going forward, the entire book is free to read online ( HTML , PDF ). Happy lisping!

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
items.content:
North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI

6 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google

FBI redacted examples of the 900 victim videos secretly recorded by North Korean hackers

State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say.

More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau.

"The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman.

This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company.

US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim.

Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software.

According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet.

Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction.

A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims.

Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities.

The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user".

"It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday.

"If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

items.title: Is there a 'right amount' of AI?
items.content:
While I’ve made my skepticism of AI clear by now, I’m not an anti-AI purist fighting against “no apps with any hint of AI coding allowed on my machine.” For one thing, it’s almost certainly a lost battle. Microsoft and Apple are both using coding agents for OS development, and while I can’t prove that most people running Linux have at least some LLM-touched code somewhere on their system, I’d be incredibly surprised if it’s not there.

Just this week, I moved back to Overcast from Castro as my podcast player. (I’ve spent a decade or so switching between them. Castro’s queue system is terrific, but the app has always been buggier than Overcast, its subscription price skyrocketed a year or so ago, and it’s now on its third owner—a shady-looking company that’s already diluted the privacy policy.) I know that developer Marco Arment has become an enthusiastic “agentic coder”, and that this means Overcast has Claude-generated code in it. Ditto his fun new app Fineliner , which I’m using on my new iPad mini (more about which later). I don’t think either of these programs are going to erase my data, make my iPad overheat, or send my credit card information to Russian hackers. In theory, what Lex Friedman wrote recently on the subject of vibe-coding, well, vibes with me:

AI has dramatically reduced the cost of producing an app, but it hasn’t reduced the work required to produce a great app. There’s a difference between generating something that works and something that works reliably, handles unexpected situations, feels intuitive, respects platform conventions, and continues improving. […] I will gladly pay for apps that feel crafted. I want apps that show refinement, testing, and thoughtfulness. I want apps from developers I trust will keep on building and iterating. I want apps from developers who feel invested—those are the ones I’m willing, even eager, to invest in.

(Note that’s Lex Friedman, who is cool, not Lex Fridman, who sucks .) And, yes, I think Marco is a developer who feels invested. He shows deep concern for code quality, to the point where he rather (in)famously eschewed using existing libraries for functions he could code himself. He wanted to understand his code inside and out.

If you haven’t heard of it, Big Walk is a game from House House, the Untitled Goose Game people, published by technically-still-Mac-developers Panic. It was a favorite for this year’s Independent Games Festival awards, but a group of IGF jurists issued a statement declaring they would “decline to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity.” They specifically refused to make a distinction between using genAI for assets (e.g., graphics and sound) and code, writing,

Programming is a creative discipline whose labour deserves the same respect we extend to any part of making a game. This extends to the past work used to train these models without the creators’ consent.

This led House House to confess that, okay, they “sparingly” used LLMs to “help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs”. Less than a percent of a percent of the code in Big Walk was touched in any way by LLMs, and they went out of their way to say “this is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal,” and that they “support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk ’s LLM usage may not meet their standards.”

Based on everything above, I shouldn’t have any issue with this. And at first, I didn’t. It all struck me as a tempest in a (Utah) teapot .

House House, an already very successful studio with not insignificant resources, made a real choice to rely on a morally abhorrent software system rather than engage the help of real people—whether in the form of paid contracting or just friendly help. I want to say this not to try to exaggerate the scope of what they did but to make it absolutely clear that there is a real, material…

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 집에서 한 말이나 제 언니랑 한 말들을 학교 가면 다 알고있어요 그래서 제가 말한 내용이랑 똑같은 내용을 꼭 제가 들을 수 있을때 언급하고 남자애들 여자애들 할것없이 제가 안보이는 데에서 조금만 이상한 말 하면 비웃으면서 지나가요 ㅠ 제가 진짜 친구가 없어서 학교에서 한마디도 안하는 날들이 대부분인데 제가 언니랑 학교 구석에서 말한 내용이랑 집에서 혼잣말 한 내용들을 똑같이 언급한게 한두번이 아니에요 ㅠ 제가 그냥 내용만 겹치면 말을 않겠는데 제가 말했던 내용 언급하면서 꼭 제 이름도 한번씩 부르고 그래요 보통 사람들은 자기이름을 그렇게 말하면 기분나빠서 한번 돌아보기라도 하겠지만 저는 성격이 워낙 내성적이라 누가 비웃고 지나가거나 째려보거나 저 보면서 한숨쉬어도 아무말도 못하거든요 ㅠ 그래서 그냥 기분만 나쁜건데 이게 하루이틀 쌓이니까 너무 힘들더라고요 ㅠ 처음엔 저도 이게 정신이 약간 아픈건가 했는데 정신병 관련 영상도 다 보고 그랬는데 환청은 이런식으로 들리는게 아니라고 하더라고요 계속 날 비난하고 그런식으로 들리는건데 저는 그런게 전혀 아니라 제가 전날 했던 얘기들, 방금 쉬는시간에 학교 구석에서 나눈 얘기들을 자꾸 똑같이 언급하니까 미치겠어요 ㅠ 한두번 우연으로 겹치는게 아니라 계속 겹쳐요 진짜.. 그리고 애초에 제가 학교에서 말을 한마디도 안하는데 자꾸 저한테 그런 반응을 보인다는게 애초에 저한테 이상한 일이 일어난다는 반증 아닌가요? 그리고 걔네가 말했던걸 몇개를 말씀드려보면 제가 도청을 의심한 초기에 급식실에서 밥먹고있었는데 어떤 남자애가 “도청” 이러고 지나가는거에요 그리고 저희반 남자애가 제 언니 이동수업반이랑 같은 반인데 거기서 쉬는시간에 “도청기를 달고다녀 ㅋㅋㅋㅋ” 이랬다는거에요 진짜 이상하죠 저는 예전에 우울증 약을 먹은적이 있어서 정신이 막 무결점으로 건강한 편은 아니에요 근데 저희 언니는 그런적도 없고 교우관계도 좋고 진짜 정신이 건강하거든요 ㅠ 근데 저희 언니가 그런말을 들었다니깐 진짜 도청이 일어나는게 맞는거구나 생각했어요.. 그리고 또 있었던 일을 말씀드리면 이동수업 때 제 뒷쪽에서 남자애가 제 아버지 직업을 언급하면서 제 이름을 말하는거에요 이게 도청을 하지 않고서는 절대 알수가 없는 사실이거든요 ㅠ 또 “정신병ㅋㅋㅋ” 하면서 제 이름을 언급하는거에요 이것도 도청을 하지 않았다면 알수 없는거고요 더 말씀드릴 사례가 많은데 그러면 너무 길어져서 이정도만 말씀드릴게요 그래서 찾아보니까 머리에 붙일수 있는 초소형 도청기가 있다길래  제 언니가 제 머리를 샅샅이 뒤져줬거든요? 근데 그래도 아무것도 안나오더라고요 ㅠ 그리고 또 도청 탐지 업체를 알아보니까 금액이 너무 비싸서요 ㅠ 제가 고3인데 이런일을 당해서 너무 스트레스 받는데 방법이 없어서 정말 어떻게 해야될지 모르겠어요 안그래도 제가 여자애들이나 남자애들이 괴롭힐 소재가 많은 조용한 애거든요 ㅠ그래서 저를 지나칠때 꼭 한마디 끼얹고 지나가고 그래서 학교생활이 막 편한 그런애는 아닌데 학교에서 유일하게 맘놓고 말할 수 있는 언니랑 말하는 얘기를 다 알고있으니까 스트레스 받아서 공부 능력도 점점 떨어지는것같고 쨋든 걱정이 이만저만이 아니에요 어떡해야되죠 ㅠㅠ 제가 성격이 활발한 편도 아니고 집에 돈이 많지도 않아서 진짜 대학 잘가야되는데 걱정이에요ㅠㅠ 긴글 읽어주셔서 감사하고요 여기가 사생활 침해 관련한 갤러리니까 혹여나 저랑 비슷한 경험이 있으시거나 관련 지식이 있는 분은 제가 어떻게 해야하는건지 알려주시면 진짜진짜 감사드릴것같아요 많은 도움 부탁드려요 정말 방법 여러가지 찾아봐도 안되겠어서 여기다 글 남겨요

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-125659 📢 Source: CERT-In 💣 CVSS Score: 2.1 (LOW) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False This vulnerability exists in the eMudhra emBridge due to missing authorization checks in the FileBrowser API endpoints. These endpoints perform file system enumeration using the LocalSystem account without adequately validating the requesting caller's authorization. An unauthenticated attacker on the same LAN could exploit this vulnerability by sending malicious webpage to the local HTTPS Web API. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to enumerate file and directory names and obtain information about the directory structure of the targeted system. The vulnerability however, does not provide access to file contents or permit file modification, deletion, or code execution, or access to cryptographic keys and hardware token PINs. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-13T10:17:45.806Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-125659
items.title_ko: CERT-In, eMudhra emBridge FileBrowser API 인가 누락 취약점 CVE-2026-125659 공개
items.summary_ko: CERT-In이 공개한 CVE-2026-125659는 eMudhra emBridge의 FileBrowser API 엔드포인트에서 인가 검사가 누락된 취약점이다. 같은 LAN에 있는 인증되지 않은 공격자가 악성 웹페이지를 통해 파일과 디렉터리 이름 및 구조를 열거할 수 있다. 파일 내용 열람, 수정, 삭제, 코드 실행, 암호화 키와 하드웨어 토큰 PIN 접근은 이 취약점으로 가능하지 않다. CVSS 점수는 2.1(LOW)이다.
items.content_ko: CERT-In이 공개한 취약점으로, eMudhra emBridge의 FileBrowser API 엔드포인트가 LocalSystem 계정으로 파일 시스템을 열거하면서 요청자의 권한을 충분히 검증하지 않는다. 같은 LAN에 있는 인증되지 않은 공격자가 악성 웹페이지를 로컬 HTTPS Web API로 보내 악용할 수 있다. 성공하면 파일과 디렉터리 이름을 열거하고 대상 시스템의 디렉터리 구조 정보를 얻을 수 있다. 다만 이 취약점으로는 파일 내용 열람, 파일 수정·삭제, 코드 실행, 암호화 키와 하드웨어 토큰 PIN 접근이 가능하지 않다. CVSS 점수는 2.1(LOW)이며, 원격 악용 가능 여부는 False로 표시됐다. 공개일은 2026-11-13이다.

items.title: Nvidia employees petition to bring back Jensen Huang
items.content:
Some Nvidia employees are calling for Jensen Huang’s return even after his multiple reported extramarital affairs and abrupt resignation , according to internal correspondence reviewed by WIRED.

An internal “suggestion box” post submitted before Huang’s resignation by a longtime engineer at Nvidia urged the company’s board to take employee sentiment into consideration prior to taking any action. The submission has attracted more than 1,600 comments since then, with several asking board members to find a way to bring back Huang.

“If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” wrote one anonymous commenter.

“We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance,” wrote another.

One employee went as far as sending a companywide email demanding transparency into Huang’s exit. “I stand by Jensen,” the staffer wrote. “Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us.”

The employee couldn’t be reached for comment, while the engineer behind the suggestion box post declined to comment.

Nvidia and its new board chair, investor Harvey Jones, didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

Huang, a 63-year-old who had led Nvidia since its founding in 1993, wrote in an email to employees on Sunday that he had been “unfaithful to [his] wife” and that there was “no excuse.” The acknowledgement followed reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset . The board announced Huang’s resignation on Thursday morning, following reports of an alleged second affair with a direct report. (This employee has not commented on the matter.) Since then, Reuters reported on an alleged affair with yet another Nvidia employee. Huang hasn’t commented about these reports since his Sunday email.

Are you a current or former Nvidia employee who wants to talk about what’s happening? We’d like to hear from you. Using a nonwork phone or computer, contact the reporter securely on Signal at peard33.24.

Nvidia’s board is largely made up of early Nvidia investors and Huang’s longtime confidants. It named Nvidia chief financial officer Colette Kress interim CEO and appointed former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones as chair of the board. The crisis has cost the company $1 trillion in market value since the allegations surfaced, prompted investigations from US lawmakers and the FBI, and raised the prospect of new export controls on chips.

It’s been business as usual inside the company throughout this week, but Huang’s resignation left many employees stunned . In the hours after, about two dozen employees posted on LinkedIn in support of Huang, with one describing their faith in his leadership as unwavering. Over the same period, WIRED couldn’t identify any posts from Nvidia employees in support of his resignation.

One employee who has been at Nvidia for a couple of years and wasn’t authorized to speak publicly says they perceive the desire for Huang’s reinstatement as widespread. They worry the company will eventually suffer without its founder at the helm and say that the board must bring him back. “Nvidia is Nvidia because of Jensen,” the employee tells WIRED.

Many employees had expected a board investigation to conclude before any big changes would occur. For instance, the suggestion-box post called on the board to share its findings with employees and formally solicit their sentiment “about Jensen’s continuing as our CEO.”

Instead, Huang left just as the inquiry had begun. Staffers are seeking to better understand why. “If America fails the man who helped build its future,” the employee in the companywide email stated, “then this world does not deserve Jensen Huang.”

items.summary_ko: WIRED가 입수한 내부 서신에 따르면, 일부 Nvidia 직원들은 Jensen Huang의 보도된 여러 건의 혼외 관계와 갑작스러운 사임에도 불구하고 그의 복귀를 요구하고 있다. 사임 전 올라온 익명 건의함 게시물에는 1,600개 이상의 댓글이 달렸고, 일부는 이사회에 Huang을 다시 데려올 방법을 찾아달라고 요청했다. 한 직원은 사임 경위의 투명한 공개를 요구하는 전사 이메일을 보냈다.
items.content_ko: 사임 전 한 엔지니어가 이사회에 직원 여론을 고려해 달라며 건의함에 올린 글에 1,600개 이상의 댓글이 달렸다. 댓글에는 “미션을 믿는다면 보스를 다시 데려오라”, “우리는 모두 사람이고 실수할 수 있다. Jensen은 좋은 일을 많이 했으니 두 번째 기회를 받아야 한다”는 내용이 포함됐다. 한 직원은 “공정함을 지키는 것이 그의 리더십이 우리에게 가져다준 것들로부터 거리를 두는 것을 의미해서는 안 된다”며 “나는 Jensen의 편에 선다”는 입장을 전사 이메일로 밝혔다. 해당 직원은 논평 요청에 응하지 않았고, 건의함 게시물을 올린 엔지니어도 논평을 거부했다. 본문이 여기서 끊겨 있어 이후 내용은 확인할 수 없다.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

items.title: Show HN: My $300 embroidery machine needed a subscription, so I built my own app
items.content:
ZigZag is a visual embroidery editor built in Rust for performance, with

built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) support so AI agents can create and

edit designs alongside you. Turn SVG artwork into stitches, fine-tune it in

the editor, and export PES, DST, EXP, JEF, or VP3 for broad compatibility

with embroidery machines—or send designs directly to a Brother Skitch

Draw in Illustrator, draw in ZigZag, or let an agent draw. The Rust engine

and zigzag command-line tool power the same workflow outside the editor.

For Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, macOS 11 or later. Open the DMG, then drag

ZigZag into Applications. The release is signed and notarized by Apple.

— the ZigZag-<version>-x86_64-windows.zip asset on the latest release.

For 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1709 or later) and Windows 11. Unzip it and

double-click ZigZag.exe . Windows SmartScreen warns on apps without a

Microsoft-trusted signature the first time they run; click More info →

Run anyway . No Rust installation is needed.

src/svg.rs SVG import (usvg): fill and stroke parts, transforms, text

src/document/ editable document; settings saved back into SVG ids,

layout edits as SVG transforms, lettering

src/params.rs stitch settings tokens + fabric presets

src/stitch/fill.rs tatami fill (scanline sections, staggered rows)

src/stitch/satin.rs satin columns: two rails, auto-satin, underlays, short stitches

src/stitch/stroke.rs running / triple-run stitch

src/boolean.rs polygon booleans and offsets (i_overlay)

src/design.rs planner: overlap removal, cap order, routing, trims

src/checks.rs digitizing checks (sizes, widths, lettering, hoop)

src/formats/ PES (+PEC), DST, EXP, JEF, VP3, Skitch PEN writers;

PES/PEC/DST/EXP/JEF readers; preview; worksheet

src/machine/ Skitch Bluetooth protocol (+ btleplug client, `ble` feature)

src/studio/ editor (egui on OpenGL via glow) + MCP server (`gui` feature)

src/mcp_bridge.rs stdio ↔ HTTP bridge for MCP clients that launch a command

cargo build --release # CLI + MCP bridge, no system deps

cargo build --release --features gui,ble # + the studio editor and Skitch upload

Linux needs the usual X11/Wayland and OpenGL dev libraries for gui . libdbus

Staggered rows, any angle, with underlay (edge walk + rows) and pull compensation

Zigzag column between two rails, with center/contour/zigzag underlay, pull compensation and short stitches on tight curves; plain, S-stitch or zig-zag top stitching; several threads across the column (multicolor satin)

Strokes (any width); Ink/Stitch-style two-rail paths with rungs; filled shapes : rings use inner/outer outline, bars/letters/crescents split at their tips (auto-satin), or border follows the outline

Rows that follow the outline inward, or one spiral out from the center (Ink/Stitch's circular fill)

E-stitch: a line with prongs into the shape

Placement line → stop → tack-down → stop → satin cover

One wandering line through the shape, quilting style: light and soft

Open running-stitch rows following the outline, or one spiral

A grid of X's, sewn as rows of half-crosses out and back

Woven stripes in several threads (a mirrored sett you edit in the panel), each thread its own color block

Satins wider than 7 mm are auto-split (shorter, staggered stitches) and

use auto spacing (narrow columns more open, wide ones denser).

Remove overlaps: fill hidden under later objects isn't sewn (keeps 0.5 mm of overlap).

Cap order: center-out, bottom-up, grouped by color, still respecting layering.

Routing: travel stitches stay inside shapes: straight across where a straight line stays inside, otherwise round the inside of the outline (Ink/Stitch's underpath), so a fill with a cut-out is sewn with few or no cuts. Trims only where neither works (up to 50 mm of travel).

Sewing control per object: a start and an end point (where the thread comes in and leaves, so the next object is close), trim after, stop after (to lay foam or trim appliqué). The document can also connect objects…

items.title: Contra "Glue work considered harmful"
items.summary: practices
items.content:
Sean Goedecke, Glue work considered harmful (emphasis here, and in the rest of the quotes, in original):

So why doesn’t glue work get you promoted, if it’s so crucial to shipping projects? Are companies stupid? Are they deliberately leaving value on the table? No, I don’t think so. Companies don’t reward glue work because they don’t want you prioritizing it. And they don’t want you prioritizing it because they want you shipping features. Glue work is hard. If you’re capable of doing glue work well, they want you to use that ability to deliver projects instead of improving general efficiency.

This is an argument to settle for mediocrity. If you’re like most people who have worked in big tech, it is plainly obvious to you that they are leaving value on the table. (Whether it is deliberate or not is a matter of what’s in people’s hearts.) What big tech employers want is largely incoherent. They want you delivering features. They also know that somebody’s got to do the glue work to keep the company running, and they have trouble describing or capturing its value.

Here, and throughout his post, Goedecke is quite accurately describing some of the incentives presented to employees at big tech. My problem with the post is that he tells you to internalize them instead of keeping in mind that a better world is possible.

The core problem is that you’re deciding for yourself what the company needs instead of doing your job. Isn’t it your job to make your team run smoother? No! Your job is to execute the mission of your company’s leadership.

If glue work is critical to the mission of a company’s leadership, how does neglecting it serve the mission?

It is better to execute that mission at 60% efficiency than to spend all your time increasing efficiency in general (or even worse, to execute some other mission at 100% efficiency). Why? For two main reasons: first, you’re inevitably going to burn out, which will be bad for everyone; second, it’s better to let your team get used to operating at the base efficiency level of the company instead of artificially removing friction for a brief period.

There are two very different things being conflated here: saving some gas in the tank for when there are real deadlines, which is great advice, versus not trying to make your coworkers’ lives better, which is a real case of misaligned incentives.

Besides, the premise is fundamentally wrong: there is a lot of glue work that, if you give it the respect it deserves, removes friction permanently . I’m obviously biased here, but I think the cargo-nextest project is a great example of glue work (running tests!) done so well that the problem mostly vanishes. More recently, at Oxide I wrote an agent skill called flake-review , backed by a catalog I wrote 1 over a few hours. I’ve since used the skill to fix almost a dozen test flakes, making the entire team’s lives better.

Should you never do glue work? No, you should do glue work tactically . That is, you should do this kind of extra work for the projects you lead — the projects whose success you’re accountable for — in order to make sure they succeed. You won’t be rewarded for the glue work specifically, but you will be rewarded for the success of the project. For other projects, you should just do your regular job.

With the most emphatic of feelings, fuck that . I do glue work whenever I’m the best situated person to do the glue work. The idea that you shouldn’t help your peers, simply because someone in middle management has trouble articulating the value of helping your peers, should be deeply offensive to any serious professional.

Is this a deeply cynical take about how to succeed in office politics? I don’t actually think so. Large tech companies operate at something like 20-60% efficiency at any given time (as they get larger, they get less efficient).

A large chunk of people’s working lives is wasted on solvable problems whose value organizations don’t recognize. How can one not be cynical…

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.title: The AI-Assisted Linux Driver for DisplayLink Gets Legal Notice
items.content:
Before we dive into the matter, you first have to understand what DisplayLink is. It is a proprietary graphics transport technology that lets computers connect to one or more external displays over USB, using docks or adapters built around DisplayLink chips.

It works by compressing display data on the host computer and sending it to a chip in the connected device. The chip then decodes it for output to monitors through interfaces such as HDMI or DisplayPort .

On Linux, this support can rub some people the wrong way due to its closed-source nature. That is where Mike Lothian 's ( FireBurn ) Vino comes in as an open alternative.

Unfortunately, Synaptics owns DisplayLink and has sent Mike cease-and-desist letters alleging that he infringed its DisplayLink patents with his project.

Vino is a driver that lets the Linux kernel talk to DisplayLink docks directly. It is meant to replace DisplayLink's closed-source software and the open source EVDI kernel module that sits beside it.

Mike wrote it with help from Claude Code, and the first version reached the kernel mailing list in June, unfinished. He had faced a communication issue between the dock and the driver and asked other developers for help.

In early July ( courtesy of LWN.net ), he emailed a Synaptics employee for guidance and mentioned his Rust rewrite of EVDI. About two weeks later, a different employee replied.

That reply said his Rust rewrite of EVDI was not a thing of concern. Rather, the concern was the DisplayLink protocol and codec, which Synaptics believes are covered by its patents.

A cease-and-desist letter followed on August 17. It told Mike to stop development and withdraw anything he had submitted to maintainers and hosting sites, with a signed confirmation due by August 28.

An appendix listed over 125 patents without saying which applied. Mike posted a working version 3 of Vino on August 26 and asked Synaptics the next day which claims they had in mind.

The answer came in October as claim charts . They map one claim from each of two patents, GB2484736 and GB2485613 , to his source code.

The October 5 letter said Synaptics would seek $25,000 for the cost of preparing those charts if Mike missed an October 11 deadline, with the figure rising by at least $25,000 each week.

Mike replied on October 6 ( message 8 ) with an offer to pause public work on the encoding code the charts point to if Synaptics paused the deadline and the weekly charge. He also asked about licensing that code for non-commercial use.

On October 7, Synaptics said it would grant no patent license or promise not to sue and set October 18 as a final deadline.

What I can see so far is a very aggressive patent infringement witch hunt against a lone open source developer who was quite open to communication.

Synaptics took about three weeks to answer his request for specifics, then followed with a potentially life-ruining $25,000 demand that compounds weekly.

Mike describes Vino as a clean-room driver and says he reverse engineered it from captured USB traffic and vendor programs.

If you didn't know, in a clean-room recreation, one party studies the original implementation, then writes a description, and a separate party builds the new code from that description alone.

It is meant to act as a defense against copyright claims because it shows nothing was copied. Synaptics’ July reply argues that clean-room or independently written code can still infringe a patent. 🤷

Vino also lands in a busy stretch for AI-assisted reverse engineering, from smart TV cleanups to office suite clones . Legal pressure has reached other AI-built projects too.

Mike has already taken down the Vino repository in response to the demands, and Synaptics has not made a public statement so far.

Only time will tell what happens to the work, and I hope someone forked it before it went offline, as that would give others a good starting point to build on.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.summary_ko: 저자는 Bun의 WebKit 포크에 있는 JavaScriptCore와 Filip Pizlo의 WebKit 블로그 글에서 영감을 받아, 여러 스레드가 같은 메모리를 공유하는 JavaScript를 구상하게 되었다. 이 방식에서는 읽기에 잠금이 필요 없고, 객체를 만든 스레드가 잠금 없이 쓰기를 하며, 다른 스레드가 쓰려 할 때만 잠금이 걸린다. 저자는 이를 세 번에 걸쳐 직접 구현했다고 밝혔다.

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Orchestrator
items.content:
Today, we’re rolling out Gemini 4 Hydrogen inside Google Antigravity alongside a new model dropdown option called Orchestrator, which pairs Hydrogen with our strongest models for long-horizon tasks, including Gemini 4 Carbon, in an optimized balance of quality, efficiency, and latency.

Selecting Orchestrator (Carbon) from the model selector in Google Antigravity.

Earlier this week, we introduced Gemini 4 Carbon alongside /swarm for tackling massive, multi-worktree engineering tasks with parallel agent teams. In just a couple of days, tens of thousands of swarms have been launched on Antigravity, pushing frontier intelligence on the hardest problems.

For everyday feature work and debugging inside a single session, running a frontier reasoning model with multiple parallel agents on every step of every routine task slows down your loop and burns frontier quota. A common industry approach is to use a static “model router” that guesses task difficulty from your first prompt and routes the entire task to the cheapest model that is good enough to complete the task. Unfortunately, these start breaking down as agents become longer running, requiring different levels of complexity at different stages, often discovered as the task evolves.

Orchestrator takes a dynamic, bidirectional approach between Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen within the evolution of a single trajectory. For example, Carbon can start in a read-only phase to explore dependencies, resolve ambiguities, and build a concrete plan with explicit re-planning triggers. Hydrogen could then take over to write edits, update packages, and run tests. If Hydrogen hits friction, it would hand back to Carbon to inspect the state, repair the plan, and resume execution. This allows Orchestrator to reach near-Carbon task success while being faster and more quota-efficient. On Terminal-Bench 4.1, Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while, on average, consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster.

Pairing Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Carbon with the Antigravity SDK for automated open-source issue triage and code generation.

Using Gemini 4 Hydrogen in Google Antigravity to upgrade dependencies, refactor shared utilities, and generate accessible image alt text.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen brings cutting-edge intelligence for everyday coding and agentic workflows. When you want frontier planning paired with speed without managing model switches, Orchestrator puts both Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen behind one prompt. Starting today, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is rolling out across paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Orchestrator is rolling out as Orchestrator (Carbon) and Orchestrator (Argon) for Google AI Ultra subscribers, and as Orchestrator (Argon) for paid Google AI Pro subscribers, with additional models and plans supported in the future. Enterprises can access both in Gemini for business .
