items.title: Paths in pieces
items.summary: unix
items.content:
Many [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7] [8] [9] Linux distributions and package managers audit just-built binaries for non-relocatable absolute paths. If a binary contains a path /path/from/build/machine , it might not run on the end-user's machine.

Now, a basic grep on the binary, or a slightly more sophisticated

using GNU binutils's strings will detect these paths, right?

The answer is no , at least when using GCC and targeting x86-64 : you should not assume that string constants end up literally in the binary.

In this C++ source we create a std::string from a string constant:

Compile with GCC 12 or later and run, which prints the path:

But the path occurs precisely 0 times in the binary itself:

Surely these bytes must be part of the binary somewhere ? Let's run strings on it and grep just for the /home prefix:

with a made-up subdirectory xbrew ? How?

The answer is that GCC optimizes our std::string{PREFIX} . The fact that we see something that looks like the prefix is merely a coincidence.

GCC splits our string up into two (overlapping) pieces of 16 bytes, like so

which fit exactly in xmm registers, so that it can copy our string to the std::string buffer using vectorized move instructions.

Filtering the relevant bits from g++ -O2 -S -masm=intel , we get

and our string is stored at .LC0 and .LC1 as constants, which just happen to be next to each other in the binary:

In general, this happens when a string constant is copied into a buffer, as with std::string , strcpy or memcpy ; strings that are only passed around as pointers, like in fopen(PREFIX "/x", "r") , stay intact.

Some package managers like Conda and Spack install packages into a padded prefix during their builds, with the idea that they can be “relocated” to a shorter prefix of the user's choice: the binaries are patched in-place. Conda uses a repeated string _placehold in a directory name to make the prefix long enough.

Now, even if we pick a 256-byte path (a convenient multiple of all x86-64 register widths) by padding the path Conda-style

and keep our fingers crossed that GCC puts the pieces of the path contiguously in the binary, we do not see our prefix back in the binary. What we get instead is a much shorter string of only 176 bytes (that is 11 times 16):

This is thanks to a further optimization: since the string _placehold repeats every 10 bytes, the 16-byte pieces repeat every lcm(10, 16) = 80 bytes, and GCC needs to store only 5 distinct 16-byte constants for the padding:

For string literals, I don't think so. Clang does not split strings into constants, yet it generates essentially the same instructions. For example, take a longer path, and target AVX2 with -march=x86-64-v3 :

Clang simply puts the string in a section dedicated to strings, .rodata.str1.1 :

and copies its 53 bytes with two overlapping 32-byte ymm loads and stores, at offsets 21 and 0:

That isn't particularly different from GCC's version, which loads the same two pieces from constants in .rodata.cst32 instead:

So what does GCC gain? In terms of performance, probably nothing measurable: both do the same loads and stores. With repeated pieces, GCC might have a slight edge, because a repeated piece is loaded once and stored multiple times (11 loads for 16 stores in the earlier example). It also uses aligned reads, but that matters only for ancient CPUs.

In terms of size, GCC's pieces can take more space than the string itself: overlapping bytes are stored twice, and the pieces are aligned to 16, 32 or 64 bytes. The 53-byte path above takes 64 bytes as two pieces, against 54 bytes as a string. It only pays off if it results in deduplication, for example when many strings share a prefix of at least 16 bytes for SSE2, 32 bytes for AVX2, and 64 bytes for AVX-512. Presumably deduplication does not save much in practice, especially now that some distributions use AVX2 as their baseline.

GCC 12 이상은 std::string{PREFIX}를 최적화해 문자열을 겹치는 16바이트 조각 두 개로 나누고, 이를 xmm 레지스터에 맞는 벡터화된 이동 명령으로 std::string 버퍼에 복사한다. 그래서 /home 접두사처럼 보이는 문자열은 우연히 나타난 것이며, 하위 디렉터리를 포함한 전체 경로는 바이너리에서 찾을 수 없다. 입력 본문은 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: Trying Tourette's device tested by Lewis Capaldi was the best day of my life
items.content:
Trying Tourette's device was the best day of my life

1 day ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google

Katie (right) and her mum Julia travelled to Nottingham from Hertfordshire to try out the device, which would help calm Tourette's symptoms

When Katie was just a child, her tics were so relentless they left her bedridden with a sore throat for two weeks.

The now 15-year-old says living with Tourette's affected her ability to sleep, eat, and caused her to miss school.

But a wrist device developed by researchers in Nottingham helped her calm down in an "instant".

Katie recalled trying it on for the first time, and said: "It was absolutely life-changing. It was like the best day of my life."

Tourette's syndrome is a neurodevelopmental condition with symptoms usually starting in childhood.

Katie, from Hertfordshire, said she first started to experience symptoms aged seven.

She said: "It was constantly moving, constantly making sounds and then I was kind of getting looked at like, 'why are you doing that?'

"I used to make snorting sounds, but it was constant all the time, so I'd give myself a really bad sore throat and then be in bed for two weeks.

"I think I became quite sad a lot of the time."

Watch the moment the device instantly stops tics for Ollie, who has a neurological condition

Katie's mum Julia said it was "heartbreaking" to see her daughter struggling.

"You feel helpless. You feel you don't know where to turn really," she said.

It was not until she read about a wrist device - developed by the University of Nottingham - that Julia felt hopeful for her daughter.

She and Katie learned more about the device, and came to Nottingham to try it in December before it was available to buy.

Katie said when she turned it on for the first time, the effect was "instant" and she became "really calm".

"And I remember on the drive home, I just cried the whole way home because I was like, 'I want it now'," she said.

Prof Stephen Jackson, who has led the research, said seeing the impact on users of the device had been "a dream come true"

Katie was among the first people to use the Neupulse device.

It works by delivering electrical pulses to the median nerve at the wrist, which trials have shown can change the activity in the parts of the brain involved in movement control.

They found that rhythmic stimulation can reduce the frequency and intensity of tics.

In 2023, a clinical trial of 121 people in the UK found they experienced, on average, a reduction in tic frequency of 25% while using a prototype of the device.

That year, it was also tested by the singer Lewis Capaldi , who has Tourette's, prior to a gig in the city.

The university added Capaldi was impressed by the effects of Neupulse and was eager to try it out again in the future.

Lewis Capaldi visited the team behind the device in 2023, prior to a gig in Nottingham

The device was developed by the university and its spin-out company Neurotherapuetics Ltd, which secured £1m in additional funding to commercialise the device.

According to the Tourettes Action charity , there are two versions of the device: Neupulse-C - which is available as a consumer wellness device - and Neupulse-M, which is intended to be marketed as a medical device specifically for the treatment of tics and Tourette's syndrome, but it has not yet received regulatory approval for this purpose.

Neupulse-M is still going through the regulatory approval process. It is hoped that if regulatory approval is obtained, the device will be considered for NHS use.

The charity added the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) had identified the technology as "promising", and had requested further evidence of its long-term benefits before making recommendations over NHS adoption.

The university said "thousands" of the devices had been sold so far.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

items.title: I'm making LLMs work on small and old devices
items.content:
Run the biggest language model you can on the smallest hardware you own.

TV boxes, old tablets, single-board computers and routers all have a CPU, some RAM and flash storage that sit idle most of the day. smolmaxxing finds the biggest model each of them can really run, then pushes it further with custom kernels, careful memory use and weights streamed from flash. Every number in this repo was measured on the device itself.

Both devices run 8B and 16B mixture-of-experts models on about 1 GB of RAM by keeping only part of each model in memory and reading the rest from flash as it's needed.

More devices (phones, single-board computers, routers) are coming. The techniques aren't tied to one box: the 1-bit kernel needs only basic NEON, and the flash streaming works on any Linux or Android device with more model than RAM.

All of it is a patch on llama.cpp . The main ideas:

Kernels built for the chip. A 1-bit lookup-table kernel, repacked 2-bit and ternary formats for the Cortex-A55, and versions of them for the A7, which has no dot-product instructions.

Less RAM per model. Most of a small model's vocabulary is rarely used, so we drop those output rows. On the TV, a "headless" mode also stops the launcher and Google services while a model runs.

Experts paged from flash. A mixture-of-experts model only uses a few experts per token. We keep the popular ones in RAM, read the others from flash on demand and prefetch the next layer's. This is how 8B and 16B models run on 1 GB.

Streaming for dense models bigger than RAM, at the flash's full speed.

docs/how-it-works.md has every technique with its measured gain.

The quickest start is a ready-made model file from Hugging Face. They need the patched llama.cpp: stock llama.cpp can't load them.

TV box or another ARMv8.2 Android device: docs/tv-box-setup.md

Jailbroken iPad on iOS 12: ipad-air/README.md

All model files and how to rebuild them: docs/models.md

MIT . The llama.cpp patches are derivatives of llama.cpp (MIT). Model weights keep their own licenses, and the evaluation texts are Wikipedia excerpts (CC BY-SA 4.0).

Built on llama.cpp and llama2.c . Models from Qwen , unsloth (GGUFs and importance matrices), PrismML (Bonsai), inclusionAI (Ling-mini-2.0), tablinum (Moon-Beam), bartowski and mradermacher (GGUFs), Google (Gemma) and stories260K . The iPad is jailbroken with Amethyst . The banner uses Archivo (SIL OFL) and is rendered by tools/banner/render.sh . The 🤏 logo is the pinching-hand emoji from Google's Noto Emoji (Apache 2.0).

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Nvidia is in turmoil after the resignation of Jensen Huang , with the CEO's departure coming after an accusation of him having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy (alongside an allegation of a second affair). Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been announced as the interim CEO to hold the Nvidia fort while the board conducts the search for a permanent replacement.

Team Green's stock has plunged during these revelations, and to say the loss of Huang is going to be felt keenly is an understatement. He was a key figure and intrinsically linked to Nvidia's success, a CEO cut from the same cloth as the likes of Steve Jobs.

He also exerted a level of control at Nvidia which was quite astonishing. Most CEOs have, what, 10 execs directly reporting to them (probably fewer). A few years back, Huang told the New York Times ( via Business Insider ) that he had around 50 direct reports in order to minimize the 'layers' in the company (meaning middle management).

Huang was also pivotal to Nvidia's entire business strategy, as analyst Ming-Chi Kuo made clear in a post on X, in terms of "deciding on aggressive spec upgrades and making them happen" based on his clout with the supply chain. Kuo observed (just prior to Huang's exit, I should clarify) that: "His value is that he weighs strategy, organization, technology, and supply chain all at once, then makes the call quickly and puts resources behind it."

Huang was clearly critical in terms of the internal workings of Nvidia as well as its broader strategy and direction. But with the CEO's departure, it's not just shareholders who should be worried – this could be the worst news for PC gamers who are already concerned about the state of play with GeForce GPUs.

Why gamers need to worry about Nvidia losing Huang

(Image credit: Nvidia) Nvidia is now in a panic, let's make no bones about that. There was no clear succession path for the CEO position by all accounts, and this has all happened very suddenly.

The interim CEO, Colette Kress, is the CFO and as such a name readily associated with Nvidia's financial wherewithal. Presumably the idea is to introduce a sense of financial stability here – a steady hand on the rudder in that respect for the time being while the board searches for Huang's full-time replacement.

Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.

Whoever that turns out to be will doubtless feel that stepping into Huang's shoes – or maybe that should be donning his leather jacket – is an intimidating prospect.

So what's the worry for PC gamers specifically? Here's how the theory runs. Even with a new CEO – whoever that replacement may be – Nvidia obviously isn't going to suddenly run dry of profits. A Reuters report quotes Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, who speculated on Huang's departure before it happened, noting that: "I don't see the next 12 to 18 months of revenue suddenly disappearing if Jensen were to leave."

However, Boloor added: "My bigger concern is next decade, because Jensen isn't simply ‌Nvidia's CEO ⁠but he's the person who has consistently identified where computing is going before customers even realise. Replacing that strategic vision ... is an enormous challenge."

Here's where matters get tricky for gamers, as guess what? The CEO who eventually replaces Huang – and indeed Kress in the interim – is going to want to ensure big profits…

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.summary_ko: YellowKey라는 제로데이 익스플로잇이 물리적 접근으로 Windows 11의 BitLocker를 우회해 암호화된 드라이브에 접근 가능하게 한다. 수 초 내에 보호를 무효화할 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 보안 연구자 Nightmare-Eclipse가 공개한 YellowKey 제로데이 취약점은 물리적 접근만으로 Windows 11 기본 BitLocker 보호를 우회할 수 있다. BitLocker는 Microsoft가 제공하는 전체 볼륨 암호화 기술로, 신뢰할 수 있는 플랫폼 모듈(TPM)에 저장된 복호화 키 없이는 디스크 접근이 불가능하도록 설계되었다. 많은 조직과 정부 계약업체에서 필수 보호 기술로 사용 중이다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

HP and Asus are moving some PC production from Thailand and Vietnam back to China as AI-driven component costs climb

The work is going to Chinese assemblers like Luxshare and Huaqin rather than Taiwan's server-focused ODMs, partly for access to Chinese memory

TrendForce expects the share of notebooks built outside China to slip from 24% to 21% this year, with no sign yet of cheaper PCs as a result of said move back to the country

HP and Asus have started moving some of their PC manufacturing out of Thailand and Vietnam and back into China, as AI-driven price increases for memory, storage, and other components eat into already-thin hardware margins.

The shift was reported by Nikkei Asia , whose reporters Lauly Li and Cheng Ting-fang cited unnamed industry sources.

Acer is also among the brands rebalancing output, while Dell , the world's third-largest PC maker, is reportedly evaluating a similar move as manufacturers chase efficiency amid ballooning bills of materials.

Reversing the China+1 strategy as memory silicon costs hit home

The move partly reverses the "China+1" strategy the industry has pursued since the first round of US-China trade tensions.

Nikkei reported in 2023 that HP planned to move a large share of its laptop production out of China, and some PC makers even explored building plants in Saudi Arabia to sidestep tariffs on Chinese-made goods. Asus told investors in August 2025 that it had already shifted more than 90% of its US-bound motherboard and PC production to Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia.

"The move is really driven by cost pressures," a chip industry executive whose company supplies all major PC makers told Nikkei. The executive added that prices have climbed sharply for far more than just memory, leaving PC makers struggling to absorb the increases, and that Chinese contract manufacturers are winning work largely because they can undercut on price.

The scale of the squeeze shows up in the bill of materials (BOM). According to TrendForce , processors, DRAM and SSDs accounted for roughly 68% of a mainstream notebook's BOM in the third quarter of 2026, up from about 45% in the first quarter of 2025.

Omdia arrives at a similar picture from a different angle, with memory and storage rising from around 15% of a PC's total price to roughly 40%, according to figures reported previously by TechRadar Pro .

The move is a bit interesting considering that relocating assembly does not make DRAM cheaper; It implies that roughly a third of the bill, plus assembly, logistics and engineering costs, is the only place a factory move can save money, unless the new factory also comes with cheaper memory.

That is, however, precisely the pitch from Chinese contract manufacturers: a supply chain manager told Nikkei that these firms are marketing better access to Chinese-made memory chips to prospective clients, and TrendForce reports that they are waiving engineering and tooling fees to win orders. China also keeps an edge in peripheral and structural parts that other countries still struggle to match, Counterpoint analyst Ivan Lam told Nikkei.

The bubble started to pop , and with it something else is also happening. I need to discuss this and address my own mind on the topic. Hence this post.

The most valuable product the leading AI companies sell is not a model. It is not a chatbot, not an API, not a reasoning engine, not a subscription. The most valuable product they sell is fear . And doom is their growth strategy.

Every time you read that a model might “ escape the lab ”, that an agent might “ deceive its operators ”, that a training run might “ self-improve past human control ”, that a superintelligence could “ end the human race ”, this is not a scientific finding; this is a marketing document in disguise. You are reading the pitch deck for the largest regulatory moat ever constructed, and the prelude to the most profitable IPO in the history of software.

This feels like conspiracy theory territory…

It is, until you follow the money, and then it sounds like the obvious reading of the room. The AI doom narrative is being deliberately cultivated because it does a few things at once. It makes the companies selling the doom look powerful and inevitable, which inflates their valuation.

It creates the political pressure for governments to write rules, and those rules, whatever their stated purpose, will not make AI safer; they will make it impossible for anyone except the fuck faces who already have all the AI built up and ready. The only escape from this trap is open weights and open code, the path China has already taken.

That may also be the only honest way to justify what these systems have already done to the world’s internet, data, and scraping. I can still see your bots ButtBook . No doom should be tolerated. No IPO should happen. This technology must be open, or it will be owned, and it will be owned by a very small, very selective bunch of rich assholes.

When I wrote about politics , I had an important question in mind. And this question still exists. “ Who benefits when the public believes AI is dangerous? ”

Freelance developer for hire with experience in Shopify and WooCommerce.

If AI were truly as dangerous as the doom narrative claims, the correct public policy response would be to stop, to halt frontier training runs, to treat the technology the way we treat nuclear enrichment… And funny enough, that’s not what the leading labs ask for.

They ask for licensing… Have a government spy on locals, seeing everything, and sharing it with no one. They ask for reporting requirements, which isn’t what they proposed. They ask for compute thresholds, and funny, there are very few ways to validate the amount of compute used. They ask for safety institutes, staffed, in practice, by people who used to work at, or who will soon work at, the very companies being regulated.

They ask for rules that will only benefit themselves and no-one else. And some of the public bought this bait . And worse, like most of the companies in this imperialist world, they see the public not as customers; the public is the raw material. Fear is how you turn the public into working hands for your own monopoly.

Consider how the doom narrative flows through the media. A former engineer at a lab writes a long essay about existential risk. A lab publishes a “ safety report ” that reads like a horror story about its own product. A CEO testifies before a legislature, and says that his own creation might one day need to be controlled by a government, and that he, humble as he is, is willing to help design the controls. 온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다
